content:
maria: Quick note — our EU-WEST GPU-hours forecast for this week just spiked. Peak hourly demand ~3.2k GPU-hours (up 28% week-over-week). Could eat into reserved capacity and force burst into other regions.
kevin: Source? which model family is driving this?
maria: Mostly chat-large and a few heavy long-context evals. Avg seq len ~1.8k tokens. I pulled this from the forecasting job (link: https://dash.redwood/forecast/weekly) — look at model_mix_v2.
raj: Oof. Are we still seeing low KV cache hit rate for those workloads? That would make per-token cost and GPU time worse.
maria: yes — cache hit ~42% on average for those runs. Also more single-request heavy concurrency (many small streams) so batching affinity is down.
lisa: Do we have headroom in other regions to overflow EU-WEST? Latency constraints for customers in EMEA are tight.
kevin: We have some spare spot capacity in europe-north (30 GPUs) but provisioning lead time for on-demand is ~12-18m for new nodes. If we rely on cross-region routing, p95 latency increases ~80ms per hop.
ops-bot: @channel Capacity-request created: CR-2026-489. Waiting for capacity-team triage.
sre_oncall: Can we tune autoscaler to reduce over-bursting and preserve steady-state while satisfying SLAs? I want config proposals we can test in canary.
maria: Proposed quick patch (canary in eu-west-1 only):
```yaml
autoscaler:
  targets:
    steady_gpu_hours: 2200           # commit to this as steady baseline
  burst_policy:
    headroom_pct: 12                # keep 12% headroom for sudden spikes
    max_burst_nodes: 36             # hard cap on temporary nodes
  prewarm:
    warm_window_minutes: 10         # start prewarm earlier for long seq workloads
  cost_controls:
    daily_cost_cap: "$12000"       # soft throttle once we hit this
    emergency_override: false       # manual only
```
kevin: That looks reasonable. Headroom 12% feels tight given provisioning lag — maybe 15%? Also set `prewarm.warm_window_minutes` to 12 for the chat-long route.
raj: If we increase headroom we should also add a cheap fallback model (quantized 4-bit) in the same region to avoid cross-region. It buys us throughput at lower latency.
lisa: Agree on fallback model. Also suggest adding a circuit-breaker metric: `burst_node_launch_failures > 3 within 5m` -> stop new bursts and notify infra pager.
sre_oncall: Good call. Can we add a small policy block for cost vs SLA tradeoff that is auditable? Example: `if daily_cost_spend > 90% of cap AND p95_latency < target*1.05 -> maintain bursts else throttle`
maria: I can draft the canary config and push to `infra/autoscaler/canary/eu-west` today. Who can validate the rollout and observe impact for next 2 business days?
kevin: I can watch dashboards and handle rollbacks.
raj: I'll wire up an eval to route 10% of heavy-seq traffic to the fallback quantized model and measure quality delta.
lisa: I'll update the runbook with the new circuit-breaker thresholds and the emergency capacity request flow.
ops-bot: Capacity-team assigned CR-2026-489 to @kevin and @maria. ETA for triage: 90m.
sre_oncall: Action items: 1) maria -> push canary config 2) kevin -> dashboard monitor + rollback play 3) raj -> fallback eval 4) lisa -> runbook update. Keep notes in the CR. We'll reconvene if burst hits again. :thumbsup:
kevin: noted. starting canary now, will post results in this thread.
